conventions.convention: The arena is an affine space over a four-dimensional real vector space V with surjective absolute-time covector τ; the spatial metric is defined only on ker τ. No spacetime norm, Lorentzian metric or speed bound is supplied.
Galilean maps use t′=t+b and x′=Rx+vt+a, with R∈SO(3). Inertial frames have fixed time vectors and positively oriented orthonormal spatial triads.

An apparatus trajectory has a nondegenerate open time interval as domain, is C² in spatial coordinates, and is parametrized by the chosen frame time. No trajectory is assigned to an unmeasured quantum particle.
Dimensions form Q⁴ on length, duration, mass and charge; reference units are m, s, kg and C. A d-dimensional position wave function has dimension length^(−d/2). Angles and phases are dimensionless.

P1 assigns nonzero separable complex Hilbert spaces. Pure preparations are rays with unit representatives; arbitrary nonzero rescaling preserves the ray, but its associated density operator uses a unit representative. General preparations are positive self-adjoint trace-class operators of trace one.

P2 uses self-adjoint operators with declared domains and units, Borel spectral probabilities, and finite bounded effect families. Means require absolute first-moment integrability; normalization alone supplies no moments.

P3 applies to finite or countable mutually orthogonal projection families with strong sum I. Conditional normalization is permitted only when the branch probability is positive; discarded outcomes are summed in trace norm.
Autonomous evolution is U(t)=exp(−itH/ℏ). The norm-differentiable Schrödinger equation holds exactly for initial vectors in D(H); driven families require separate assumptions.

The baseline massive model has m>0, finite spin s∈{0,1/2,1,…}, componentwise maximal position and momentum domains, and real bounded measurable potential on the componentwise W²,² Hamiltonian domain. Singular potentials, boundary models and radiation are separate assignments.
The CCR is an identity on the image of Schwartz functions in L², which is a graph core for each position and momentum operator; no unrestricted identity of unbounded products is asserted.
Spin and statistics are declared species assignments, including the trivial spin-zero representation; no nonrelativistic spin-statistics theorem is claimed.

Independent identically distributed repetitions are additional sampling assumptions. Apparatus identifications and measured inputs carry uncertainty into downstream conclusions; agreement with data is evidence about combined assumptions.

load_bearing.statement: For declared massive-matter systems, adopt nonzero separable complex Hilbert spaces, unit rays as pure preparations, density operators as general preparations, trace-norm probability mixtures, and completed Hilbert tensor composition of independent distinguishable subsystems, assuming Countable Choice.

Assuming Countable Choice and Choice, adopt self-adjoint sharp observables with declared units and outcome law μρᴬ(B)=tr(ρEᴬ(B)), equal to ||Eᴬ(B)ψ||² for unit pure preparations; finite bounded effects summing to I have probabilities tr(ρFₐ). Moment existence is separately conditional on integrability.

Fix rational-exponent dimensions on length, duration, mass and charge, SI reference units, the exact SI defining constants h, c and e with ℏ=h/(2π), experimentally determined μ₀, and the listed quantity dimensions and types.

Assuming Countable Choice and Choice, an isolated autonomous system has a declared self-adjoint energy operator and evolves by U(t)=exp(−itH/ℏ); vectors evolve continuously, the Schrödinger equation holds exactly on the operator domain, and density operators evolve by unitary conjugation.

Assuming Countable Choice and Choice, adopt the Newtonian arena and Galilean inertial frames, classical apparatus trajectories, and for m>0 and finite spin s the space L²(R³;C^(2s+1)), componentwise position and momentum operators, and the bounded-real-measurable-potential Hamiltonian on componentwise W²,².

Assuming Countable Choice, adopt symmetric or antisymmetric completed-tensor sectors for declared species and the displayed finite-spin SU(2) representation with Sᵢ=ℏJᵢ, including the trivial spin-zero representation; species assignments are model inputs.

For a declared finite or countable orthogonal projection measurement resolving I, adopt probabilities pₐ=tr(ρPₐ), conditional update PₐρPₐ/pₐ for pₐ>0, and trace-norm discarded ensemble ΣₐPₐρPₐ. The rule is restricted to the declared ideal class.

Comparisons with recorded data require declared preparation, isolation, detection and sampling models; iid repetitions are additional assumptions, apparatus identifications carry uncertainty, and deductions using measured inputs inherit their qualifications.
Assuming Countable Choice, for d≥1 and ℏ>0 the Schwartz classes are invariant common cores for Qⱼ and Pₖ, their products are defined there, and (QⱼPₖ−PₖQⱼ)f=iℏδⱼₖf for every Schwartz class f.
The Galilean parameter map is injective, each map is bijective with the displayed inverse, composition has the displayed parameter law, and the maps form a subgroup of the bijections of R×R³.

concerns.concern: Step 1.3 says zero acceleration is preserved 'by clause 1' of lem-cm-adapted-charts-and-galilean-transformations. Clause 1 gives coordinate transformations; the differentiated acceleration law and zero-acceleration equivalence are clauses 2 and 3. The deduction is sound, but the clause locator is inaccurate.

The page's displayed item order places inertial-frames and classical-apparatus-trajectories before quantities-and-units, although both definitions depend on quantities-and-units. It also places P5 before its prerequisite P6. The prose explains the P6-before-P5 order, but the rendering inventory does not follow it. This is a supplier-before-consumer exposition defect.

alerts.finding: Fact F6 states the CCR and cites 'lem-nrqm-framework-ccr-on-the-schwartz-core clause (a)'. Clause (a) establishes Schwartz invariance and domain membership; the commutator identity is clause (b). The identity itself is supplied, but the locator is wrong.

Definition (f) says 'The parameter a of a translation has the unit of length u_H'. Definition (a) assigns u_H to the energy observable, and the cited autonomous-dynamics definition explicitly calls it an energy unit. Translation parameters have length units under def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units, so u_H is the wrong symbol here.

Definition (a) permits s=0, but Definition (c) states 'S_± are not self-adjoint.' At s=0, P6 and prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices give J_x=J_y=0, hence S_+=S_−=0. The zero operator is self-adjoint. The assertion as written fails in an explicitly admissible sector.
